newsitem.title: USA: Brooklyn Union, Lilco finish negotiations.
newsitem.headline: Brooklyn Union, Lilco finish negotiations.

text.p: Negotiations between Brooklyn Union Gas Co, Long Island Lighting Co and the Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) have been completed, Brooklyn Union spokesman Bob Mahony said.

The resulting proposal for LIPA to acquire Lilco's electric transmission and distribution system, substantially all of its regulatory assets and its share of the Nine Mile Point 2 nuclear power plant through a stock purchase from a holding company to be formed by Brooklyn Union and Lilco is now pending before New York State's Public Authorities Control Board, Mahony said.
He said the proposal has not been presented to Brooklyn Union's board.

When the tentative agreement was announced, the companies also noted the proposal would have to be approved by the New York State Public Service Commission, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission and the Securities and Exchange Commission.
There were no major changes in the terms announced March 19, Mahony added.

The original proposal called for LIPA to pay about $2.5 billion, resulting in proceeds to the holding company of $1.7 to $1.9 billion after payment of taxes and short-term liability. It also called for LIPA to assume about $3.6 billion of Lilco debt.

The proposed holding company would own Brooklyn Union's present operations, Lilco's natural gas distribution system, non-nuclear electric generating assets and certain other assets. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
